obligations.direct_check: The two coordinate centers are distinct and q≥2. Their exceptional divisors are smooth, connected and disjoint.
Projection from either center resolves on its blowup and pulls back over the other blowup, where that projection is already regular.

Off the exceptional divisors rho embeds. On each exceptional divisor tau_i embeds tangent directions and d rho detects the normal direction; point separation follows as well. Compactness gives the asserted graph embedding.
Pulling the one-center identity back over the other center gives O(E_i)=rho*O(1) tensor tau_i*O(-1) without an extra exceptional factor.
Each canonical norm is the corresponding projective point-distance ratio, extended across the exceptional divisor; its zero divisor is exactly E_i.
The product metric has theta=2 alpha+eta_1+eta_2, and subtracting 2 eta_1+2 eta_2 leaves gamma_1+gamma_2.
kappa is a pullback of the product Fubini–Study form by the graph embedding. Omega=4 pi*kappa+7 omega_F is positive.
Each unscaled log(R_i^2+T^3) has lower bound -2 pi*alpha-3 omega_F from the O(2,3) sum-of-squares numerator. Summing yields -4 pi*alpha-6 omega_F.
The logarithmic analytic poles admit local psh extension after a smooth quadratic correction; the global lower curvature inequality extends as a current.
Each log-sum is at least 2 log R_i, hence phi≥pi*psi, including poles.
Poincare–Lelong gives beta+2[E_1]+2[E_2] positive, with beta=gamma_1+gamma_2 semipositive.
Locality off the two divisors gives beta^q. Both it and the non-pluripolar measure give their union zero mass.
[beta]=2H-E_1-E_2, H^q=1, mixed H/E_i intersections vanish, E_i^q=(-1)^(q-1), and E_1 E_2=0.
Expansion gives 2^q-2, strictly positive for every q≥2. The q=1 zero-mass situation is excluded.
Both resolved projections are constant on the strict transform of the line joining the centers, including its endpoints.
The smooth residual has zero integral on that curve; every smooth dd^c correction has zero integral by Stokes, precluding a positive form.
At E_i×o the other norm stays positive, so the other log-sum is smooth. Positive smooth units yield log(|z|^4+|w|^6)+O(1).
The selector is smooth off the disjoint union of E_i×o. There are no simultaneous crossing-pole charts in this model.
c_i=p_i=2, b_i=3, a_i=2/3; the strict condition ell+1>2m-2/3 is exactly ell≥2m-1 for integers ell≥0.
I(m psi)=O(-2m(E_1+E_2)) because both logarithmic coefficients are integral.
The generic witness forces divisor order 2m-1 at each E_i, using the existing crossing band and its checked semipositive extension.
Those divisor orders suffice in every exact pole chart by the radial integrability lemma; boundedness handles every other point.
Dividing a global A^m section by s_1^m s_2^m gives an O(2m) section off two codimension-q points. Local Hartogs extends it; the identity theorem recovers the original section.
The extended projective section of point order n_i has generic exceptional order m+n_i after the fixed factor. There is no Jacobian twist because B is the original base.
Reference orders become m,m; selected orders become m-1,m-1, including m=1. Disjoint-support ideal products equal their intersections.
Zero orders are discarded; if all are zero the evaluation target is zero and the dimension formula is unchanged.
A hyperplane avoiding the finite point set exists and trivializes O(d) at all centers.
L_ik vanishes at x_k but not x_i; Q_i therefore imposes all other point orders while remaining an invertible jet at x_i.
Truncate b_i/Q_i at degree j_i-1 in the local polynomial jet algebra. Multiplication restores the prescribed jet.
Degree Q_i T_i is at most sum j_k-1≤d. Homogenization in the common affine trivialization preserves every prescribed jet.
The target counts all monomials of total degree below j_i in q variables, binomial(j_i+q-1,q); surjectivity gives exact dimensions.
For d=2m, sums 2m and 2m-2 both satisfy the explicit interpolation condition. No arbitrary larger-order independence is asserted.
Subtract twice the jet count from binomial(2m+q,q) for each space; selected uses m-1 and reference uses m.
Pascal gives 2 binomial(m+q-2,q-1), asymptotic 2 m^(q-1)/(q-1)! with positive constant.
m=1 selected orders are zero and the defect equals two; the zero binomial convention handles the reference/selected formulas.
For q=2, W dimension is (m+1)^2 and V dimension m^2+4m+1, giving defect 2m.
Both dimensions have leading coefficient (2^q-2)/q!, matching the actual positive reference mass.
The nonzero defect proves the semipositive-band O(m^(q-1)) bound cannot uniformly improve to little-o. It does not settle general P21 necessity.
On a fiber over E_i the potential is finite away from o and minus infinity at o, so it cannot agree up to bounded difference with any descended base potential.
